explanations: send() creates each request's carrier span with startSpan's default parent, the tracer's current span. But send runs from the setImmediate (or the full-batch flush) scheduled inside whichever request happened to enqueue first, so AsyncLocalStorage's current span is that request's span. Every carrier span in the batch becomes a child of the first request, in its trace, and the other requests show none. The fix captures tracer.current() in labelFor, while still inside each caller's context, stores it with the pending item, and passes it explicitly as the parent when the span is created. Async context only flows along the call chain that scheduled the work, so batched or queued work has to carry each item's context with it.
